excludedLeads.text: The possibility that the closeout publication, when it appears, accounts for the $6.6 million through aggregated categories rather than named recipients, which would make the two named households a partial picture rather than the whole one.

The possibility that the 23-day standard in the closeout is measured from a different starting point than the Council's C115 order, which would make the verification technically compliant but substantively short.

The possibility that the remaining $20.6 million is the real story — that the disbursement pace slows or accelerates depending on what the closeout reveals, and that the charter renewal vote in C117 is where that pace gets set.

limits.rule: The Packet is what you know, not the fence around what you may write. The approved facts and the ledger are canon: never contradict them, and never import real-world Oakland (its people, businesses, landmarks, troubles). Everything else — the scene, the street, the weather in the room, unnamed people and what they say, new in-world places and businesses, what the city is talking about — is yours to invent; that colour is the job, and it never rewrites a canon fact. A named ledger citizen speaks only in their approved quote or their own page line. Do not brief the record. Open on a person or place living the condition.
